standard_prerequisites.name: The regular-model situation, the topological genus of a numerical type and the geometric genus of a curve
standard_prerequisites.statement: The situation fixes a discrete valuation ring, a smooth projective curve over its fraction field, a regular proper model and the components of the special fibre with their multiplicities; the numerical type attached to the fibre carries a topological genus formed from the number of components and the positive intersection pairs. For a proper curve over a field the geometric genus is the dimension of the first cohomology of its structure sheaf, and it can also be read off from the normalisation of the curve together with the singularities of the reduction. The author's own definitions of the chapter and the results of the Algebraic Curves and Varieties chapters that the proof quotes are the allowed inputs.
standard_prerequisites.use: The counted lemma is one half of the genus formula of the section, its companion giving the reverse inequality; together they identify the genus of the curve with the topological genus of the special fibre.

core_obligations: Set up the comparison: since the special fibre has a smooth rational point, the curve is geometrically reduced and its reduction has the same geometric genus, so the assertion reduces to a comparison between the first cohomology of the reduction and the sum of the topological genus and the geometric genus of the fibre (source lines 5448-5460).

Relate the two genera along the reduction map: the reduction has the same geometric genus as the fibre, which the chapter's results on genus under base change and under normalisation make explicit, and the difference between the topological genus of the numerical type and the genus of the reduction is accounted for by the singular points of the reduction (source lines 5460-5500).

Identify the contribution of the singularities: writing the reduction as the scheme-theoretic union of its components and using the exact sequence that compares the structure sheaf of the union with those of its parts, the author counts the dimensions contributed by the finite set of singular points and matches them with the difference computed above (source lines 5500-5530).

Conclude the inequality: the numerical identity obtained from that count is precisely the asserted lower bound, so the first cohomology of the reduction dominates the topological genus plus the geometric genus (source lines 5530-5538).

proof_roadmap.step: Reduce to the comparison between the two genera, using the rational smooth point hypothesis.
Invoke the genus results under base change and normalisation to fix the geometric genus of the reduction.
Count the contribution of the singular points through the union exact sequence.
Identify the resulting identity with the asserted inequality.

difficulty_reason: 计数单元是 Stacks Project 章 models.tex 的 Lemma lemma-genus-reduction-bigger-than（源 5431-5446 行，证明 5447-5538 行，92 行）：在正则模型情形下，若 X_k 有点 k-有理且在 X_k→Spec(k) 上光滑，则 dim_k H^1((X_k)_red, O) ≥ g_top + g_geom(X_k/k)。关键操作不是例行核验：证明要先借「有理光滑点 ⇒ 几何既约」把 g_geom(X_k)=g_geom((X_k)_red) 归约掉（5448-5460 行）；再用本章的基变换/正规化亏格结论把约化曲线的几何亏格算出来（5460-5500 行）；随后把 (X_k)_red 写成其分支的 scheme-theoretic union，用并集与各分支结构层之间的正合列**数出奇点贡献的维数**，并与 g_top 与约化亏格之差对齐（5500-5530 行）；最后把得到的数值恒等式认成题设不等式（5530-5538 行）。难点在于「奇点贡献」这一项必须与拓扑亏格的定义（分支数 + 正相交对数）逐项对上；原文位置在证明的 5448-5460、5460-5500、5500-5530、5530-5538 行。
